skill.name: crafting-effective-readmes

skill.summary: Guides README creation, updates, reviews, and section choices by project type and audience.

content.value_statement: Generic READMEs often miss the needs of contributors, teammates, or future maintainers. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through audience questions, templates, and quality checks.
actual_capabilities: Selects README sections for open source, personal, internal, and configuration projects.
Guides users through creating, adding, updating, and reviewing README content.
Provides templates for OSS, personal, internal, and XDG configuration READMEs.
Checks for common README gaps such as missing install steps, examples, and stale content.
Uses reference material on Standard README structure and practical README writing.
limitations: Does not verify claims unless the agent can inspect the project files.
Does not replace full product documentation or API reference generation.
Templates require user-provided project details before final README text is accurate.
Internal README guidance may need local security and compliance review.

use_cases.title: Launch an Open Source Project
use_cases.description: A maintainer creates a README with install, usage, contributing, and license sections for new contributors.

use_cases.title: Document an Internal Service
use_cases.description: A team lead creates onboarding notes, local setup steps, architecture context, and runbook sections for teammates.

use_cases.title: Refresh a Personal Project README
use_cases.description: A developer updates stale text, adds examples, and explains what they learned for portfolio readers.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a New README
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a README for this project. Ask me what type of project it is, who will read it, and the quickest successful usage path.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Missing Section
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my current README and help add a section for installation, usage, contributing, or another gap you find.

prompt_templates.title: Update After Project Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: I changed this project and need the README updated. Compare the README with the project files and propose clear edits.

prompt_templates.title: Audit for Audience Fit
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this README for its target audience. Check section order, missing context, stale claims, examples, tone, and project-type fit.

output_examples.input: User asks for a README for a new open source CLI tool.
output: Questions about audience, install path, core command, license, and contribution policy.
A README outline with title, description, installation, usage, contributing, and license sections.
A follow-up prompt asking what else should be highlighted.

output_examples.input: User asks to refresh an internal service README.
output: A stale-section review based on the current README and project files.
Suggested updates for local setup, architecture notes, ownership, runbooks, and troubleshooting.
Clear notes where team-specific details are still needed.

output_examples.input: User asks whether a personal project README is portfolio ready.
output: A review of audience, project purpose, screenshots, usage examples, and learning notes.
Specific edits that make the project easier to scan and understand.
A concise final checklist for publication.

best_practices: Start by naming the target readers and their first successful task.
Use the smallest section set that answers real project questions.
Keep setup, usage, and examples current with the inspected project state.
anti_patterns: Using an open source template for every project without checking the audience.
Writing broad feature claims without examples or setup steps.
Leaving stale commands, links, or ownership details after project changes.

faq.question: What types of READMEs does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports open source, personal, internal, and configuration project READMEs.

faq.question: Can it update an existing README?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review the current README, identify stale sections, and propose focused edits.

faq.question: Does it inspect project files automatically?
faq.answer: It can use available agent file access when the user asks for accuracy checks.

faq.question: Is it only for open source projects?
faq.answer: No. It includes different guidance for team services, personal work, and configuration folders.

faq.question: Does it write full API documentation?
faq.answer: No. It helps README content and can link to deeper API documentation when needed.

faq.question: How does it avoid generic README text?
faq.answer: It starts with audience, project type, and the quickest useful path before drafting sections.
